page.layout: One column of running text, full width; below the last line, right-aligned, the catchword "EPIST."; running head at the top, centred over the text; page number at the head, left. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: quamquam characteres eosdem esse fac-
ile judicarem, in omnibus tamen fere dis-
similitudinem aliquam deprehendi,
sed multo majorem in libello quodam
Romae recens Italice excuso, quem ante
paucos dies raptim legi. Sed literam Tau
de qua in opusculo tuo docte disputas,
hac semper forma [illegible, ~1 letters] in eo Codice effi-
ctam video, quae parum ad crueem mihi
pertinere videtur. Unum vir doctissi-
me, te plurimum rogatum velim, idmo-
do tibi non sit oneri futurum, ut cum
otio abundabis, inscriptiones Siclorum,
de quibus mentionem facis, iisdem, qui-
bus scripti sunt, characteribus exscribi-
cures, & ad me mittere non graveris:
editionem Pentateuchi Samaritani jussu
Illustrissimi Cardinalis Berulli meditor;
inscriptiones ejusmodi coeptum meum
plurimum adjuvabunt: Preces meae pa-
rum civiles, ne temerarias dicam, vide-
ri possunt, qui adeo repetita amicitia tua
abutar; sed eas ut spero, facile
excusabunt & tuum in litteras studium, & tua in me humanitas.

page.notes: The letter after "forma" is a Samaritan letter (Tau, as the text discusses) that I cannot reproduce reliably, so it is marked illegible. "crueem" is printed for "crucem" (a printer's error, left as printed). "exscribi" ends a line with no printed hyphen before "cures"; written as "exscribicures" per the rule, though the printer may have omitted a hyphen. "dif-" at the line end before "fimilitudinem" is read as "dis-" (long s), giving "dissimilitudinem". The catchword "EPIST." is right-aligned below the text.
